comparator.name: Medische Natuurwetenschappen
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from VU Amsterdam's current official curriculum overview for Medische Natuurwetenschappen (Medical Natural Sciences) at s0 (fetched for the 2026-2027 academic year), which names the same first-, second- and third-year course list documented in detail (with EC weights) in the VU Faculty of Science's programme overview/Teaching and Examination Regulations for Medische Natuurwetenschappen retrieved via s2 (edition: 2017-2018). The 2026-2027 studiegids.vu.nl page and the current-year OER PDF for this specific programme could not be located through the available web tools after repeated attempts (search and direct navigation of studiegids.vu.nl); this is recorded as a material source-currency limitation. The current curriculum-overview webpage (s0) independently confirms that the identical course names -- Inleiding medische natuurwetenschappen, Calculus, Medical (Patho)Physiology I/II, Biochemie, Klinische en Analytische Chemie, Programming for MNW, the two Fysica courses, Mathematische methoden, Organische Chemie, Practicum bio-analytische chemie voor MNW, Project zenuw-werk, Basics of Systems Biology, Moleculaire diagnostiek, Differentiaalvergelijkingen, Introduction to Bioinformatics, Van quantum tot molecuul, Optica en optisch waarnemen, Statistiek, Project kanker, and the year-3 minor/free-choice structure, M-variant orientation and bachelorproject -- remain current, so the EC weights and structural detail from the 2017-2018 programme overview are used as the best available formally adopted source for a coherent 180-EC pathway. This normalized target names no formal route/specialisation, and current official evidence confirms only a generic curriculum with a small number of internal choices, so no route is recorded. Year 1 (60 EC) is entirely compulsory. Year 2 (60 EC) is compulsory except for one course chosen from a fixed pair (Geschiedenis van de natuurwetenschappen or Maatschappelijke aspecten van de natuurwetenschappen, 3 EC each); the first-listed alternative was selected as the neutral tie-break consistent with the official ordering. Year 3 reserves a genuine 30-EC open elective/minor space in semester 1 (preserved as open space rather than instantiated with invented content; the programme's own official minor here is Biomedische Beeldvorming, but students are free to choose any minor), followed in semester 2 by two compulsory courses (Vectorcalculus, Voortgezette Biostatistiek, 3 EC each), one compulsory choice-of-one period-4 course selected from a menu that partly prepares for master specialisations (the generic Oriëntatie op de M-variant, 6 EC, selected as the least specialised, most general option under the official menu, since choosing a specialisation-named alternative such as Gezondheidszorgsystemen or Introduction to Systems Biology would favour one specific master direction with no basis for preferring it), and the bachelor's thesis/capstone in its generic 12-EC variant (Bachelorproject Medische Natuurwetenschappen) rather than one of the specialisation-named 18-EC variants (e.g. Bioinformatics/Genomics, Biomolecular Sciences, Medical Physics, Medical Physiology, Molecular Clinical Diagnostics), together with the resulting 6-EC extra free-choice course that the official curriculum explicitly permits when the 12-EC project variant is chosen ('als voor 12 studiepunten wordt gekozen is er ruimte voor een extra vrije keuze van 6 ec'), filled here with the generic academic-skills elective Wetenschapscommunicatie voor Bèta-onderzoekers rather than a specialisation-specific elective. These choices complete exactly 30 EC in year-3 semester 2 and the full 180-EC pathway, and were made before any UCR course was considered.

Explicit integration of physics, chemistry, mathematics and computing with physiology in a medical context
How disease works at the molecular and physiological level, covered through biochemistry, pathophysiology and molecular diagnostics
Medical diagnostics and imaging as core applications across the programme
Translating fundamental science into clinical applications, shown in third-year research projects
Experimental laboratory research, laboratory safety and physics/chemistry practicals
Scientific research design and reporting, taught explicitly from the first year
Medical physiology and pathophysiology taught across the first two years
Biochemistry and organic chemistry as part of the first-year scientific foundation
Clinical and analytical chemistry as a required first-year subject
Programming for medical science, applied in the nervous-system project
Mechanics, electricity and magnetism in a health/medical context
Systems biology as second-year biomedical content
Molecular diagnostics as a dedicated second-year subject
Introduction to bioinformatics for analysing biological and medical information
Optics and optical observation as second-year topics
Statistics tailored to Medical Natural Sciences
Thermodynamics and connections from quantum phenomena to molecules
Societal aspects, philosophy and ethics of the natural sciences

questions: How can more information be extracted from MRI scans about conditions such as Alzheimer's?
How can technology help surgeons identify and remove tumour tissue more precisely?

alternatives.label: Biomedical Science, Mathematics & Data Analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by the ten-course UCR life-science/biomedical cluster (molecular cell biology, human physiology, biochemistry, life science laboratory, molecular pathology and genetics, functional anatomy, pharmacology, infection and immunity, mechanisms of disease) combined with a six-course mathematics cluster and a three-course computing/data-science cluster, with neuroscience, research-methods and ethics courses in a supporting role. The label names the biomedical core first, matching the closest feasible response to VU's integration of medical and exact sciences, and 'Mathematics & Data Analysis' names the curriculum's other genuinely load-bearing strand; it does not claim the physics or chemistry content that UCR does not offer and that the completed 24-course curriculum therefore honestly omits.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to VU's Medische Natuurwetenschappen bachelor: the full UCR life-science/biomedical cluster (molecular cell biology, human physiology, biochemistry, life-science laboratory, molecular pathology and genetics, functional anatomy, pharmacology, infection and immunity, mechanisms of disease) combined with a substantial mathematics cluster (mathematical methods, linear algebra, computational and numerical methods, advanced calculus, linear systems, probability and statistics), an introductory data-science and computer-vision pairing for bioinformatics and medical imaging, neuroscience courses for the nervous-system project, and shared statistics/experimental-methods and ethics courses. It reproduces the programme's molecular/physiological disease-mechanism core, its mathematics and computing components, and its diagnostics/imaging and nervous-system themes as far as UCR allows, and leaves VU's physics and chemistry sequence (mechanics, electricity and magnetism, thermodynamics, quantum-to-molecule physics, organic and analytical chemistry) as an honest gap, since UCR offers no physics or chemistry curriculum.
progression: Formal prerequisites are respected throughout: HCBGATE101 (Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine) is completed in semester 1 before every HCBLIFE and HCBBIOM course, and DISGATE102 (Mathematical Methods) is completed in semester 2 before every DISMATH course. Introductory (level-1) courses are concentrated in semesters 1-2: Personal & Professional Development, Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, Introduction to Programming, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Mathematical Methods, and Introduction to Data Science open the programme before the specialised life-science, mathematics and biomedical courses that build on them. Advanced (level-3) courses are concentrated in semesters 2 and 4-5: Infection & Immunity and Mechanisms of Disease in semester 2, Linear Systems in semester 4, and Molecular Pathology & Genetics, Pharmacology and Probability & Statistics in semester 5, so that the molecular-disease and quantitative-methods strands both culminate after their respective foundations (the life-science laboratory and physiology courses; the mathematics gateway) are in place. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 1, within Year 1. Every course is offered in its assigned semester.

blocks: Both are the programme's introductory foundation course. Inleiding medische natuurwetenschappen orients students across the exact and medical sciences; Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine covers the life/health/biomedicine portion of that same introductory foundation.

Medische natuurwetenschappen en samenleving addresses the societal position of the field specifically. UCR's closest philosophy/ethics course is already matched to Wijsgerige vorming, and no other UCR course offers the same societal-position framing, so no counterpart is claimed.
Fysica: Electriciteit en Magnetisme voor MNW is a dedicated physics course. UCR offers no physics curriculum, so no counterpart is claimed.
Fysica: Mechanica voor MNW is a dedicated physics course. UCR offers no physics curriculum, so no counterpart is claimed.
Klinische en Analytische Chemie is a dedicated chemistry course. UCR offers no chemistry curriculum, so no counterpart is claimed.
Organische Chemie is a dedicated chemistry course, distinct from the biochemistry already matched elsewhere. UCR offers no chemistry curriculum, so no counterpart is claimed.
Natuurkunde en gezondheid is a dedicated physics course. UCR offers no physics curriculum, so no counterpart is claimed.
Natuurkunde practicum 1 is a dedicated physics laboratory course. UCR offers no physics curriculum, so no counterpart is claimed.
Thermodynamica is a dedicated physics course. UCR offers no physics curriculum, so no counterpart is claimed.
Van quantum tot molecuul is a dedicated quantum-physics course. UCR offers no physics curriculum, so no counterpart is claimed.
Both are the programme's calculus component. Calculus covers the first-year exact-science mathematics; Advanced Calculus is the direct UCR counterpart.
Both are the programme's general mathematical-methods component, matched directly by name and content.

Differentiaalvergelijkingen covers systems of differential equations; Linear Systems covers systems of linear equations describing dynamic relationships, the closest available UCR counterpart to this mathematical-systems content.

Practicum Natuurkunde en Informatica is a combined physics-and-informatics practical. Introduction to Programming directly addresses the informatics half of this practical; the physics half remains an honest gap since UCR offers no physics curriculum.
Life science and biomedical disease mechanisms
Both are the programme's dedicated biochemistry course, matched directly by name and content.
Both are the programme's physiology component. Medical (Patho)Physiology I is the first-year physiology sequence; Human Physiology is the direct UCR counterpart.

Both are the programme's laboratory-practical component. Practicum bio-analytische chemie voor MNW trains bio-analytical laboratory skills; Life Science Laboratory trains general life-science laboratory skills, the closest available UCR counterpart.

Moleculaire Diagnostiek covers molecular diagnostic techniques; Molecular Pathology & Genetics covers the molecular pathology and genetic testing that underlies such diagnostics, a direct disciplinary match.
Medical (Patho)Physiology II covers disease processes affecting organ systems ('patho-'); Mechanisms of Disease directly addresses the mechanisms of disease that this component teaches.

Project kanker is an integrative project on cancer formation, diagnosis and treatment. The UCR courses most directly relevant to disease mechanisms and molecular pathology are already matched to other components; no remaining UCR course meets the standard for a specific cancer counterpart without stretching a merely thematic connection, so no counterpart is claimed.
Inleiding bioinformatica 1 introduces bioinformatics; Introduction to Data Science is the closest available UCR counterpart, since UCR offers no dedicated bioinformatics course.

Optica en optisch waarnemen covers optics and optical observation; Image Processing & Computer Vision is the computational analogue of optical observation, the closest available UCR counterpart given UCR offers no physics-based optics course.
Both are the programme's dedicated statistics course. Statistiek is tailored to Medical Natural Sciences; Probability & Statistics is the direct UCR counterpart.

Project zenuw-werk combines nervous-system lectures, brain dissection and programming; Introduction to Brain & Behavior is the direct UCR counterpart to the nervous-system/brain component of this integrative project.
Philosophy, ethics and history of science
Wijsgerige vorming: natuurwetenschappen, filosofie en ethiek covers the philosophy and ethics of the natural sciences; Ethics is the direct UCR counterpart.
Geschiedenis van de natuurwetenschappen is a dedicated history-of-science course. UCR offers no history-of-science course among the included courses, so no counterpart is claimed.

The 30-EC year-3 elective/minor space (a coherent minor, such as the official Biomedical Imaging minor, or individually chosen units of education) is genuinely open profiling space with no fixed content specified by VU. It is preserved as open space and not matched to any UCR course.

Vectorcalculus is a dedicated vector-calculus course. UCR offers no course covering multivariable/vector calculus (line and surface integrals, divergence and curl) among the included courses, so no counterpart is claimed.

Voortgezette Biostatistiek is a dedicated advanced-statistics course. UCR's statistics course is already matched to Statistiek; no remaining UCR course addresses advanced biostatistics specifically, so no counterpart is claimed.
Oriëntatie op de M-variant is a generic internal orientation toward master specialisations with no disciplinary content of its own; no UCR counterpart is claimed.

The Bachelorproject Medische Natuurwetenschappen is a 12-EC independent research capstone. No scheduled UCR course is a thesis; UCR's standardised Optional independent research element is shown in this row instead, consistent with researchComponentId.
Wetenschapscommunicatie voor Bèta-onderzoekers is a dedicated science-communication elective. UCR offers no science-communication course among the included courses, so no counterpart is claimed.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns all seven generator-eligible Direct programme interest rows describing the programme's central, integrated identity: developing technology for healthcare, combining physics, chemistry, mathematics and computing in medicine, how disease works at molecular and physiological levels, medical diagnostics and imaging, translating fundamental science into clinical applications, experimental laboratory research, and scientific research design and reporting. UCR can implement the biomedical, mathematical, computational and neuroscience portions of this integrated identity through its life-science/biomedical cluster, mathematics cluster, data-science/computer-vision pairing and neuroscience courses, while UCR's complete absence of a physics or chemistry curriculum leaves the exact-science half of that same identity as an honest, explicitly recorded gap rather than a fabricated substitute. The one remaining generator-eligible row -- Biomedical Imaging, evidenced as a Stable study direction because it is presented as a possible structured third-year minor -- is assessed as its own coherent candidate direction rather than folded into an omnibus bucket. However, VU's own official Biomedische Beeldvorming minor is built on medical-physics content (medical image-processing physics, microscopy and spectroscopy, mechanics and thermodynamics in the cell), not on data science or artificial intelligence; the enriched UCR course database contains no physics, imaging-physics, microscopy or spectroscopy course of any kind. Building this candidate would either duplicate the Image Processing & Computer Vision course already used in the closest match as the complementary contribution to the diagnostics/imaging core item, or would misrepresent a different discipline (data science/AI) as a substitute for the physics-based medical-imaging content that UCR does not teach, which the course-selection rules explicitly prohibit. Because the next and only remaining candidate fails on insufficient evidence rather than on a manufactured distinctness shortfall, production stops at one included alternative.

notes.text: The Medische Natuurwetenschappen bachelor includes a substantial sequence of physics courses (mechanics, electricity and magnetism, thermodynamics, quantum-to-molecule physics) and chemistry courses (organic chemistry, clinical and analytical chemistry) integrated with medicine. At UCR, students can study the biomedical, mathematical and computational strands of this combination in depth, but UCR offers no physics or chemistry curriculum, so this UCR alternative does not reproduce the same depth or sequence in the exact-science half of the programme.
